newsitem.title: MEXICO: Bital says 95-96 deposit growth 44 pct.
newsitem.headline: Bital says 95-96 deposit growth 44 pct.

text.p: Banco Internacional (Bital) expects its 44-percent 1996 deposit growth to continue in 1997, a bank executive said on Wednesday.
"Total desposit growth rose from 41.192 billion pesos in 1995 to 59.50 billion pesos in 1996, a rise of 44 percent, which we expect to maintain in 1997," said Bital Vice-President Adolfo del Valle.
Del Valle said that Bital had a capitalization ratio of 15.5 percent, well above the legal minimum of eight percent.

Regarding past-due loans, del Valle said, "we have past due loans 100-percent covered by reserves. We will drop the level of reserves to 65 percent in 1997, in line with international accountancy practices."

New accountancy practices more in line with international standards came into force in Mexico on Jan 1, 1997. Equity analysts say one of the main effects of the new guidleines will be to increase estimates of past-due loans, and force banks to increase reserves.
